title: Rapid customer liaison & hotfix procedure for canary quality decline
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Runbook and coordination plan for customer-facing escalations when a model canary shows a quality regression. Covers rapid mitigation, hotpatch strategy, tenant-aware partial rollbacks, verification checks, and communication templates for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Mitigation path available that reduces customer-facing error/regression rate by >=80% within 30 minutes for Hosted and Dedicated.
Hotfix PR created and validated against canary prompt set with automated smoke tests for all deployment types.
Customer communication sent to affected tenants with ETA and rollback decision within 45 minutes of confirmed regression.
Post-incident postmortem and remediation tickets created within 72 hours with root cause analysis and follow-ups assigned.
mitigation_steps: 1) Triage: Confirm regression using canary metric dashboard (model-quality, hallucination-rate, top_logit_shift) and correlate with deployment/time window.
2) Scope: Identify affected routes, models, and tenant slices (use tenant tags in trace logs and route-level telemetry).

3) Immediate traffic controls: Apply per-route circuit-breaker to stop new canary traffic; reduce canary percent to 0% for Hosted; suspend next-step rollout in Dedicated autoscaler; notify Private customers of paused rollout.

4) Quick fallback: Route affected traffic to last-known-good model variant (pinning) for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private, coordinate a signed rollback artifact and provide steps to customer SRE for emergency rollback.
5) Hotfix branch: Create hotfix branch from release tag, add minimal change (prompt template patch, tokenization normalization, or model-compat shim). Run local smoke evals against golden prompt set.
6) Validation: Run smoke tests in a staging canary with representative tenants (shadow mode). Verify KPIs: generation latency, rejection rate, top-5 token divergence.
7) Deploy hotfix to canary slice with progressive traffic ramp and automated rollback on KPI breach (>10% error delta).
8) Customer liaison: Assign a single point of contact for each affected customer and provide ETA + mitigation details; include rollback and verification steps.
9) If hotfix fails or is infeasible, execute coordinated rollback across environments (see rollback_preconditions).
rollback_preconditions: Canary degradation confirmed by two independent metrics (quality metric and error-rate or latency spike).
Last-known-good variant is still available and tested against cohort-specific prompt set.
No pending DB/schema or KMS changes that would make rollforward impossible.
Customer-facing notifications prepared and vetted by Legal/Support for Private deployments that require customer action.
Approval from on-call SRE and product lead for cross-region rollbacks when tenant data-residency is in effect.
verification_checks: Token-level parity check on representative prompts (detect tokenization regressions).
KV-cache integrity: verify no cache poisoning or mismatched KV-version between variants.
Latency SLO check: rolling 1m p95 must not exceed baseline + 20% post-change.
Quality delta: canary prompt set mean preference score recovers to >=95% of baseline.
Shadow traffic validation for 15 minutes with zero customer-facing errors before increasing traffic to 25%.
crossenv_notes: Hosted: fastest path — pin traffic, push hotfix to canary cluster, validate, ramp. We can change routing immediately via control plane.
Dedicated: reserved GPU pools require coordination with capacity ops; use tenant-aware slices to isolate rollback to affected customers when possible.

Private: cannot push artifacts without customer sign-off. Prepare signed rollback artifacts and step-by-step technician instructions; schedule emergency maintenance window and use remote-runplay if permitted.
Data residency: do not move tenant traffic across regions for rollback without Compliance approval.
Mixed fleets: when a tenant uses both Dedicated and Private, coordinate with account manager for phased rollback to avoid split-brain behavior.
communication_templates: INITIAL: We are investigating an unexpected drop in model quality on route <route>. We've paused the rollout for your tenant and are routing you to the previous model variant. Estimated follow-up: 30-45 minutes. (SRE on-call: <name>, PM: <name>)
FOLLOWUP: Hotfix deployed to canary and validated on shadow traffic; starting progressive ramp. Expect normal behavior within 15 minutes. Please report any anomalies to <support-link>.
PRIVATE-CUSTOMER: We have prepared a signed rollback artifact and recommend an emergency maintenance slot. Please confirm readiness for a technician-assisted rollback. Contact: <AM name>

postmortem_actions: Root cause analysis: determine whether regression originated from model weights, tokenizer change, or runtime kernel swap.
Improve pre-rollout gating: add tenant-sliced shadowing and expanded golden prompt coverage for future canaries.
Automation: add automatic pin-and-notify action when canary-quality falls below threshold to reduce mean time to mitigation.
Documentation: update Private deployment rollback checklist and include sample signed-artifact verification steps.
